title: A shared groundwater threshold gave no clear runoff prediction gain at 35 Victorian catchments in 2010-2021
abstract: We test whether a common threshold in lagged groundwater anomaly predicts later rain-adjusted runoff. We use a published Victorian catchment-year panel, fit on 1988-2009, and test 274 rows from 35 catchments in 2010-2021. Training-only blocked validation selected a continuous hinge at -1 m. Against catchment intercepts, rain history and a known post-1997 offset, test mean squared error fell by 1.28%. The conditional 95% catchment interval was -2.26% to +4.31%; the time-block interval was -1.45% to +4.65%. The hinge added only 0.30% over linear groundwater. Other time splits gave small error increases. Thus this common anomaly threshold gave no clear later prediction gain. This does not exclude stream-aquifer disconnection. Regional bore anomalies are not stream-side hydraulic head. The sample is small, retrospectively selected, and has missing years. Fixed-fit intervals omit training and source uncertainty. Code, hashes, aggregate evidence and an independent audit support reproduction. External records and record-level predictions stay outside the signed package.

display.caption: Groundwater terms gave no clear later error reduction. Separate catchment and time intervals hold model fits fixed.
